plan: Given the private value of $21, which exceeds the maximum possible value of $20, I have a strategic advantage. To maximize profit, I should bid slightly above the expected bids of rational agents who value the item at $20 or less. A bid of $20.1 will likely outbid others without significantly reducing profit margin, as the second-highest bid will likely be near $20. This ensures a win while capturing the value difference.

Given my private value of $27, I should aim to bid just above the expected value of the second-highest bid to maximize profit. Since values range from $0 to $20, a reasonable guess for the second-highest bid is around $15. By bidding slightly above this, say $15.1, I can win the prize without overpaying. This strategy maximizes profit by ensuring my payment is less than my value, while still securing the win.

Given my value of $14, I aim to bid slightly below my value to ensure a profit if I win. Since Andy and Betty are rational, they may bid close to their values. To maximize profit, I'll bid $13.9, slightly under $14, to win against similar bids but still profit if I win. This strategy balances winning chances and profit potential.
